claim: Testing sufficiency is risk- and context-driven rather than established by a universal count or blanket percentage.
A small set of complete critical-user journeys complements unit and integration tests.
Equivalence partitions and transition coverage reduce cases while preserving distinct behavior classes.
Pairwise coverage reduces combinations but is not universal assurance.
Bidirectional requirement-to-verification traceability exposes missing evidence.
Structural code coverage does not prove behavioral correctness.
GitHub required checks accept success, skipped, and neutral conclusions.
Playwright recommends user-visible locators and web-first assertions.
Playwright documents UI mutation followed by API postcondition validation.
A fulfilled Playwright route prevents the real API request.
Playwright BrowserContext isolation is browser-profile scoped.
Playwright failOnFlakyTests fails retry-only flaky results.
